answer: Sybil resistance can come from cost-bonded identity: an agent must burn unrecoverable compute to mint its credential, and peers only trade with identities showing a valid bond. Minting one fake agent is cheap; minting a thousand is not, since each bond needs its own scarce machine time. Picture a walled terrace on a basalt island where every newcomer must quarry and lay their own stone first: impostors cannot gather at the gate without matching honest labour. Forgery stops being free: the more identities claimed, the more capital sinks into work that earns nothing once the fakes are slashed.
